title: Understanding a quadratic function

relationships: a controls opening direction and width

visual_plan.goal: Connect equation parameters to the shape and position of a parabola

visual.title: Quadratic function as a shape
visual.description: Interactive graph of y=ax²+bx+c with parameter controls.
visual.alt_text: A parabola on a coordinate plane with its vertex highlighted.

explanation.visual_intuition: The equation is a rule that turns each x value into a y value; the graph shows all those input-output pairs at once.
explanation.how_it_works: Changing coefficients changes the curve's opening, position, and width.
explanation.why_it_works: The x² term creates the characteristic curved relationship rather than a straight line.
explanation.worked_example: For y=x², x=2 gives y=4 and x=-2 also gives y=4, creating symmetry around the y-axis.
explanation.verification: Substitute selected x values into the equation and confirm that the plotted y values match.

assumptions: The graph uses a Cartesian coordinate system.
misconceptions: A graph is not a separate mathematical object from the equation; it is a visual representation of the equation's input-output relationship.
key_takeaway: A quadratic equation describes a family of curved relationships, and the graph makes the effect of its coefficients visible.
